text.title: The Best Series of the Year
paragraphs: It's December, and it's time for our list! These are the five series our [[readers]] loved most this year.
Number one is Night Shift, the most popular show of the year. This hospital drama is the funniest and the saddest series on our list, sometimes in the same episode.
Number two is Harbor Town, the best mystery series this year. The last episode had the biggest [[cliffhanger]] of the season.
Number three is Green Valley, the most [[relaxing]] show on TV. Nothing dramatic happens, and that's why people love it. It's perfect for the end of a long day.

Number four is Code Red, the [[scariest]] series of the year. Don't watch it alone at night! And number five is Kitchen Kings, the cheapest show to make, but one of the most fun. Ten home cooks [[compete]] to win $50,000.
And the worst series of the year? We won't say. But it had the longest and most [[boring]] episodes of all!

scariest.note: scary = assustador; the scariest = o mais assustador

boring.note: Cuidado: bored = entediado (a pessoa); boring = entediante (a coisa).

grammar.title: Superlativos: o mais, o melhor, o pior
explanation: Para dizer que algo é "o mais" de um grupo, usamos o superlativo, sempre com the: the funniest series, the most popular show.
Adjetivos curtos ganham -est: big → the biggest (dobra o g), sad → the saddest, long → the longest. Os que terminam em -y viram -iest: funny → the funniest, scary → the scariest.
Adjetivos longos usam the most: the most popular, the most relaxing. Para "o menos", usamos the least: the least boring.
Os irregulares seguem o comparativo: good → better → the best, bad → worse → the worst.
Depois do superlativo, usamos of para um período ou grupo (of the year, of all) e in ou on para um lugar (in the world, on TV, on our list).
Comparativo ou superlativo? O comparativo compara duas coisas (cheaper than). O superlativo destaca uma entre três ou mais (the cheapest).
